subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should session-stored `/exec` defaults continue to override later global/per-agent exec policy, or should global/per-agent policy become authoritative after config changes?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but current docs and tests also describe `/exec` as session-scoped persistent behavior, so changing precedence is a security/product contract decision.

options.title: Make config authoritative
options.body: Change precedence or add a migration/reset path so later global/per-agent exec policy wins over stale session exec fields.

options.title: Keep session `/exec` persistent
options.body: Document the operator recovery path and leave session entries as explicit per-session exec defaults.

options.title: Add explicit reset controls first
options.body: Keep current precedence until an operator-facing Doctor or session reset command can clear stale exec fields safely.

recommendation.title: Make config authoritative
recommendation.body: Change precedence or add a migration/reset path so later global/per-agent exec policy wins over stale session exec fields.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the `/exec` session override behavior and recently refactored the current resolver/docs surface.
